It has paved trails, botanical gardens, a Pioneer Village, a petting zoo and a miniature train ride, which are included with park admission.

attractions.description: Day trip · about 140 km from Birmingham. Solemn, mostly outdoor memorial from the Equal Justice Initiative commemorating victims of racial terror lynching; best for older kids and teens. Part of the Legacy Sites, which also include the separate Legacy Museum.

attractions.name: U.S. Space & Rocket Center

hotels.name: The Admiral Hotel Mobile
hotels.description: A stylishly updated, retro-modern hotel in the historic district, with a great pool and chic mid-century Southern hospitality.

attractions.name: USS Alabama Battleship Memorial Park

attractions.name: Dauphin Island

attractions.description: 120-acre natural park right downtown with an easy 2-mile loop trail and sweeping views over the lake — plus small swimming beaches along the way.

attractions.name: Silverwood Theme Park
attractions.description: Billed as the Northwest's largest theme park, Silverwood has more than 70 rides, slides, shows and attractions, including four roller coasters, Boulder Beach Water Park and a steam engine train.

attractions.name: Farragut State Park
attractions.description: 4,000 acres on Lake Pend Oreille with swimming beaches, hiking and biking trails; the park was once the site of a WWII naval training station.

attractions.name: Route of the Hiawatha
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Coeur d'Alene. 15-mile all-downhill rail trail through 10 tunnels and 7 towering trestles, gentle enough for kids, with shuttle rides back to the top.

cities.name: Indianapolis
cities.description: Indiana's bustling state capital celebrated for the Indianapolis 500, vibrant downtown canal walks, world-class children's museum, and active Jewish community.

chabad.name: Lubavitch of Indiana – Chabad Center for Jewish Life

groceries.name: Kroger (86th St & Township Line Rd)
groceries.description: Chabad of Indiana's visitor guide points kosher shoppers to the Kroger at 86th St and Township Line Rd, describing it as having 'a very large selection of kosher foods.'

attractions.name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis
attractions.description: The world's largest children's museum: five floors of hands-on exhibits including Dinosphere with dinosaur fossils, a carousel, and a planetarium.

attractions.name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum
attractions.description: See Indy 500-winning race cars, the Borg-Warner Trophy, and take a track tour around the famous 2.5-mile oval.

attractions.name: Indianapolis Zoo
attractions.description: A triple-accredited zoo, aquarium, and botanical garden with an International Orangutan Center, dolphin shows, and animal feeding experiences.

attractions.name: Indiana State Museum
attractions.description: Hands-on, family-focused museum of Indiana's natural and cultural history, in the heart of White River State Park downtown.

attractions.name: Conner Prairie
attractions.description: Interactive living-history park with a recreated 1830s village, costumed interpreters, a tethered balloon ride, and hands-on science areas.

attractions.name: Turkey Run State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Indianapolis. State park near Marshall in western Indiana with deep sandstone ravines and scenic Sugar Creek. Trails range from easy walks to rugged ladder climbs, with a suspension bridge and steppingstones along Sugar Creek.

cities.name: South Bend
cities.description: Historic Northern Indiana city home to the University of Notre Dame, the Studebaker Museum, and a dedicated glatt-kosher market and bakery.

groceries.name: Midwest Premium Kosher

groceries.description: Glatt-kosher deli and fully kosher grocery and bakery under South Bend Kosher supervision, carrying meat, chicken, dairy, challah, bagels, rugelach, and a full line of kosher groceries.

attractions.name: Studebaker National Museum
attractions.description: Three floors of gleaming Studebakers, vintage carriages, and the carriage Lincoln rode to Ford's Theatre.

attractions.name: Fort Wayne Zoo
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from South Bend. AZA-accredited zoo in Fort Wayne with over 1,000 animals, giraffe feedings, and a red panda exhibit (Red Panda Ridge).

attractions.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
attractions.address: 1100 North Mineral Springs Road, Porter, IN 46304
attractions.description: Day trip · about 65 km from South Bend. 15 miles of Lake Michigan beaches, towering sand dunes, and 50 miles of trails through dunes, wetlands, and prairies.

attractions.name: Shipshewana Trading Place Auction & Flea Market
attractions.address: 345 S Van Buren St, Shipshewana, IN 46565
attractions.description: Billed as the Midwest's largest flea market, this outdoor market in Shipshewana is the size of 30 football fields. Open Tue & Wed, May–Sept, 8am–4pm. Antique, livestock and horse auctions run weekly year-round. Free admission; parking $5.

cities.name: Bloomington
cities.description: Picturesque southern Indiana college town home to Indiana University, scenic forested hills, limestone architecture, and active Chabad Jewish student life.

attractions.description: Indiana's largest state park: the "Little Smokies" with a fire tower lookout, 70 miles of trails, and famous fall colors.

attractions.description: Restored 1814 pioneer village with a working limestone gristmill, cave boat tours, and the Gus Grissom astronaut memorial.

attractions.name: Marengo Cave
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Bloomington. U.S. National Natural Landmark with two guided walking tours through crystal-filled rooms, plus gemstone mining and cave-themed kids' activities.

attractions.name: Corydon Capitol State Historic Site
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from Bloomington. Indiana's first state capitol, a Federal-style limestone building built 1814-1816 that served as the capitol from 1816 to 1825. attractions.address: 3027 East South Street, Lincoln City, IN 47552
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Bloomington. Walk the pioneer farm where Abraham Lincoln grew from age 7 to 21, with a working living-history farm and visitor center.

attractions.name: Holiday World & Splashin' Safari
attractions.address: 452 E Christmas Blvd, Santa Claus, IN 47579
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Bloomington. Family-owned theme and water park with top-ranked wooden coasters, world-record water slides, and free parking, drinks, and sunscreen.

attractions.name: Clifty Falls State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 100 km from Bloomington. Rugged limestone canyon carved by Clifty Creek near Madison, overlooking the Ohio River, with several waterfalls, a fossil-filled creek bed, hiking trails, a campground, a nature center and the Clifty Inn.

cities.name: Des Moines
cities.description: Iowa's dynamic capital on the Des Moines River, renowned for the gold-domed State Capitol, botanical gardens, and Maccabee's kosher deli.

attractions.description: Hands-on science museum in downtown Des Moines featuring interactive exhibits, live science programs, a planetarium, dome theater, and a Makers Studio where visitors can try experiments.

attractions.name: Greater Des Moines Botanical Garden

attractions.description: Dome conservatory of tropical plants and orchids on the Des Moines River, with outdoor gardens including a water garden, plus hands-on kids' activities.

attractions.name: Covered Bridges of Madison County
attractions.description: Six historic covered bridges on a free, self-guided scenic byway through rolling Madison County farmland, open year-round with no admission fee; you can walk through most of them.

cities.name: Iowa City
cities.description: Vibrant university town and UNESCO City of Literature on the Iowa River, home to the University of Iowa and an active Chabad student and community center.

attractions.name: National Mississippi River Museum & Aquarium
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Iowa City. Smithsonian-affiliated, 14-acre riverfront campus in Dubuque, Iowa, with catfish and sturgeon aquariums, river otters, raptors, historic boats including the William M. Black dredge, and a 4D theater.

attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from Iowa City. 1,400-acre river-bluff park with 16+ miles of hiking trails, river overlooks, the Julien Dubuque Monument, and the E.B. Lyons nature center.

attractions.name: Field of Dreams Movie Site

The field is open sunrise to sunset year-round, weather permitting. On select days you can play catch with the Ghost Players.

attractions.name: Maquoketa Caves State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 80 km from Iowa City. Iowa's most unique state park: 13 explorable caves, a natural bridge, and balanced rock along six miles of trails — bring a flashlight.

attractions.description: Day trip · about 65 km from Wichita. Space museum and science education center featuring a planetarium, a two-story dome theater, interactive exhibits, and a re-created rocket lab.

In winter they go to Waumbek Station (4,000 ft) instead of the summit.

attractions.name: McAuliffe-Shepard Discovery Center

attractions.name: West Side Market
attractions.description: Historic public market opened in 1912, home to about 60 small businesses selling produce, meats, seafood, baked goods, and prepared food in a landmark building in Cleveland's Ohio City neighborhood.

attractions.name: The Holden Arboretum
attractions.description: Arboretum of more than 3,600 acres with gardens, trails, lakes and forest, a 500-foot Murch Canopy Walk built 65 feet above the forest floor, and the 120-foot Kalberer Emergent Tower.

attractions.name: Ohio's Amish Country
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from Cleveland. Rolling farmland of the world's second-largest Amish settlement — horse-drawn buggies, cheese factories, bakeries, and craft shops.

attractions.name: Perry's Victory and International Peace Memorial
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Cleveland. A 352-foot Doric column on Lake Erie in Put-in-Bay, Ohio, marking the War of 1812's Battle of Lake Erie, with an observation deck offering views of Lake Erie, nearby islands, and Canada.

attractions.name: Cedar Point
attractions.description: Known as "America's Roller Coast," Cedar Point features 18 roller coasters on a Lake Erie peninsula in Sandusky, Ohio, plus a mile-long beach, boardwalk, and family ride areas.

cities.name: Columbus
cities.description: Vibrant state capital and university powerhouse featuring scenic riverfront parks, world-renowned science centers, and an active Jewish community.

groceries.name: Kroger Bexley / Columbus
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.name: COSI
attractions.description: Voted the nation's #1 science museum by USA Today's 10Best, COSI offers hands-on STEAM exhibits, a planetarium, and live science shows for all ages.

attractions.name: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
attractions.description: Victorian glass Palm House, global plant biomes, a children's garden, and Dale Chihuly glass art.

attractions.name: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium
attractions.description: Zoo and aquarium near Powell, north of Columbus, home to about 10,000 animals. Features Polar Frontier (polar bears and Arctic foxes), a hands-on tide pool, a reptile house, a kangaroo walkabout, and the Wildlights holiday LED light display.

attractions.name: Hocking Hills State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 70 km from Columbus. Waterfalls, caves, and sandstone gorges like Old Man's Cave and Ash Cave, with family-friendly trails.

cities.name: Cincinnati
cities.description: Historic Queen City on the Ohio River, celebrated for historic architecture, hilltop parks, and deep Jewish institutional heritage.

groceries.name: Kroger Blue Ash Kosher Department
groceries.description: Full-service supermarket with a dedicated kosher deli, meat, and dry goods department.

attractions.name: Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden
attractions.description: The nation's second-oldest zoo, home to famous hippos like Fiona, and a popular Festival of Lights in winter.

attractions.name: National Underground Railroad Freedom Center
attractions.description: Powerful riverside museum on the Ohio River tracing the fight for freedom from slavery to today.

attractions.name: National Museum of the U.S. Air Force
attractions.description: Day trip · about 85 km from Cincinnati. The world's largest military aviation museum, at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base near Dayton, with more than 350 aerospace vehicles and missiles, including presidential aircraft. Admission and parking are free.

cities.name: Oklahoma City
cities.description: Oklahoma’s capital combines rich Western heritage, modern cultural districts, and a warm Jewish community.

chabad.name: Chabad Community Center of Oklahoma
chabad.address: 3000 W Hefner Road, Oklahoma City, OK 73120

groceries.name: Trader Joe's
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.name: Oklahoma Route 66 Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Oklahoma City. Official state museum tracing the Mother Road decade by decade, from Dust Bowl migration to the heyday of roadside diners and motels.

attractions.name: Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Oklahoma City. Nearly 60,000 acres of ancient granite mountains and mixed-grass prairie with free-roaming bison, elk, and longhorns, plus hiking and a visitor center.

attractions.name: Oklahoma City National Memorial & Museum
attractions.address: 620 N Harvey Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73102
attractions.description: Outdoor memorial and museum honoring victims of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, featuring the Field of Empty Chairs and the Survivor Tree.

attractions.name: Myriad Botanical Gardens
attractions.address: 301 W Reno Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73102
attractions.description: 15-acre botanical garden in downtown Oklahoma City with the Inasmuch Foundation Crystal Bridge tropical conservatory (ticket required), Mo's Carousel, water features, and outdoor grounds that are free and open daily 6am-11pm.

attractions.name: National Cowboy & Western Heritage Museum
attractions.description: America's premier institution of Western history, art and culture, featuring cowboy art, Native American galleries, and a new immersive 360-degree exhibition on the American West.

attractions.name: Oklahoma City Zoo and Botanical Garden
attractions.description: 130-acre AZA-accredited zoo with 2,000+ animals, expedition-style habitats, and a dedicated children's zoo.

attractions.name: Science Museum Oklahoma
attractions.description: One of the nation's largest science museums, with 390,000 square feet of hands-on exhibits, a planetarium, and live science shows.

attractions.name: First Americans Museum
attractions.address: 659 First Americans Blvd, Oklahoma City, OK 73129
attractions.description: Celebrates the collective stories of Oklahoma's 39 tribal nations through immersive galleries, family programs, and a discovery center for kids.

attractions.name: Chickasaw National Recreation Area
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Oklahoma City. A national recreation area in the Arbuckle Mountains near Sulphur, Oklahoma: mineral springs, swimming holes, waterfalls, bison pastures, and a nature center.

cities.name: Tulsa
cities.description: Known for world-class Art Deco architecture, green river parks, and a vibrant community anchored by Chabad of Oklahoma.

attractions.name: Woolaroc Museum & Wildlife Preserve
attractions.description: Oil baron Frank Phillips's 3,700-acre ranch with a world-class Western art museum, herds of bison and elk, and a scenic drive through the Osage Hills.

attractions.name: Oklahoma Aquarium
attractions.description: Public aquarium in Jenks, a suburb of Tulsa, home to what it calls the world's largest collection of bull sharks, viewed from a walk-through shark tunnel. Visitors can also touch sharks and stingrays.

attractions.name: Gathering Place
attractions.address: 2650 S John Williams Way, Tulsa, OK 74114
attractions.description: Tulsa's 66-acre riverfront park with large playgrounds, gardens, boat rentals, and picnic areas — free to enter.

attractions.name: Philbrook Museum of Art
attractions.description: A 1920s oilman's Italianate villa housing world art and Native American collections, ringed by 25 acres of formal gardens.

attractions.name: Discovery Lab
attractions.description: Tulsa's hands-on children's museum near the Arkansas River and Gathering Place, offering STEAM exhibits and programs for young kids and families.

attractions.name: Tulsa Zoo
attractions.description: Zoo in Mohawk Park with more than 2,000 animals. Exhibits include Lost Kingdom, Sea Lion Cove, Africa, Chimpanzee Connection, African Penguins and a Children's Zoo. There is also a Safari Train and a carousel.

attractions.name: Woody Guthrie Center
attractions.description: Archives-based museum celebrating the Okemah-born folk singer's life and message, with handwritten lyrics and rotating music exhibits.

attractions.name: Natural Falls State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Tulsa. A 77-foot waterfall cascading through a mossy Ozark valley, with short family trails, yurts, and a disc golf course.

attractions.name: Robbers Cave State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 140 km from Tulsa. Historic outlaw hideout site in the San Bois Mountains of southeast Oklahoma, featuring a sandstone cave, cliffs popular with rappellers, hiking trails, a lake, and cabin/lodge lodging.

cities.name: Portland
cities.description: Lush Pacific Northwest metropolis surrounded by mountain peaks, vibrant parks, and an active Jewish community.

groceries.name: Safeway (Barbur Blvd)
groceries.description: Supermarket carrying kosher dry goods, certified meats, and holiday essentials.

attractions.name: Fort Clatsop
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Portland. Replica of the 1805–1806 Lewis and Clark winter encampment with a visitor-center museum, films, ranger programs, and trails.

attractions.name: Columbia River Maritime Museum
attractions.description: Day trip · about 120 km from Portland. Wave-shaped waterfront museum in Astoria showcasing historic vessels and the seafaring heritage of the Columbia River and the "Graveyard of the Pacific."

attractions.name: Haystack Rock
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from Portland. Towering 235-foot sea stack with tidepools full of starfish and anemones at low tide, plus nesting puffins and seabirds.

attractions.name: Ecola State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from Portland. Scenic headland park with old-growth forest trails, sweeping ocean viewpoints, and access to secluded coves.

attractions.name: North American Aerospace Museum
attractions.address: 500 NE Captain Michael King Smith Way, McMinnville, OR 97128
attractions.description: Major aviation and space museum (formerly Evergreen Aviation & Space Museum) housing the Spruce Goose and 150+ aircraft and spacecraft.

attractions.name: Oregon Coast Aquarium
attractions.address: 2820 SE Ferry Slip Rd, Newport, OR 97365
attractions.description: Day trip · about 150 km from Portland. Aquarium in Newport, Oregon, on Yaquina Bay featuring sea otters, sharks, a walk-through tunnel, seabird aviary, and touch pools.

attractions.name: Oregon Zoo
attractions.description: Zoo with elephants, condors, primates, and conservation programs in Washington Park.

attractions.name: Portland Japanese Garden
attractions.description: Traditional 12.5-acre garden with eight garden styles, walkways, streams, a tea house, and views of Mount Hood.

attractions.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
attractions.description: Hands-on science museum with a planetarium, giant-screen theater, and tours of the USS Blueback submarine.

attractions.name: International Rose Test Garden
attractions.description: Free public garden with over 600 rose varieties blooming across terraced beds in Washington Park.

attractions.name: Lan Su Chinese Garden
attractions.description: Ming-dynasty-style walled garden in Portland's Old Town Chinatown, with a central lake (Lake Zither), koi, and a teahouse (Yun Shui Teahouse) offering tea tastings and cultural programs.

attractions.name: Powell's City of Books
attractions.description: Powell's City of Books claims to be the world's largest independent new-and-used bookstore, filling an entire city block in Portland's Pearl District.

attractions.name: Silver Falls State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 70 km from Portland. Oregon's largest state park, home to the Trail of Ten Falls where visitors can walk behind several waterfalls.

attractions.name: Tillamook Creamery
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Portland. Working cheese factory offering a free self-guided tour of the cheese-making process with samples and views of the production floor.

attractions.name: Multnomah Falls
attractions.description: Oregon's tallest waterfall at 620 feet, with a historic lodge, visitor center, and trails including the famous Benson Bridge overlook.

cities.name: Bend
cities.description: Sunny high desert outdoor hub featuring scenic river trails, alpine lakes, and community services from Chabad of Central Oregon.

groceries.name: Fred Meyer Kosher Corner
groceries.description: Supermarket with kosher grocery dry goods, grape juice, and holiday items.

attractions.name: High Desert Museum
attractions.description: Museum near Bend, opened in 1982, featuring live native wildlife, art, and indoor and outdoor exhibits on the natural and cultural history of the West's High Desert.

attractions.name: Crater Lake National Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 140 km from Bend. The deepest lake in the U.S., famed for its intense blue water, 33-mile Rim Drive, overlooks, and hiking trails.

attractions.name: Painted Hills
attractions.description: Day trip · about 110 km from Bend. Striking red-and-gold striped fossil beds in the John Day Fossil Beds National Monument, with short trails and overlooks.

attractions.name: Smith Rock State Park
attractions.address: Smith Rock State Park, Crooked River, OR 97760
attractions.description: Dramatic river-canyon cliffs and spires popular for hiking, mountain biking, and rock climbing.

cities.name: Philadelphia
cities.description: The historic Birthplace of America, featuring cobblestone alleys, premier cultural museums, and bustling Jewish community centers.

attractions.name: Hershey's Chocolate World
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Philadelphia. Free chocolate-making tour ride plus build-your-own candy bar and other interactive chocolate attractions in Hershey, PA, known as "the sweetest place on earth."

attractions.name: Hersheypark
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Philadelphia. Chocolate-themed amusement park in Hershey, PA with roller coasters, family rides, a water park, live shows, and ZooAmerica, plus chocolate-related attractions.

attractions.name: Dutch Wonderland
attractions.description: Day trip · about 90 km from Philadelphia. "A Kingdom for Kids": a family amusement park near Lancaster with over 35 rides, attractions, and shows, plus Duke's Lagoon water play area. Designed for kids 12 and under.

attractions.name: Strasburg Rail Road
attractions.description: Day trip · about 85 km from Philadelphia. America's oldest continuously operating standard-gauge railroad; authentic steam-locomotive excursions through Amish farmland near Strasburg, PA, with themed trains seasonally.

attractions.name: Independence National Historical Park
attractions.description: The Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, and surrounding historic district where the nation was founded — free to walk, timed tickets for Independence Hall.

attractions.name: Please Touch Museum
attractions.address: 4231 Avenue of the Republic, Philadelphia, PA 19131
attractions.description: Hands-on children's museum in historic Memorial Hall (a National Historic Landmark) with interactive play zones and rotating family exhibits.

attractions.name: Philadelphia Zoo
attractions.description: America's first zoo, home to many rare and endangered animals, with Zoo360, a campus-wide network of see-through mesh trails that let animals roam through treetops and over visitor pathways.

cities.name: Pittsburgh
cities.description: The City of Bridges boasts world-class universities, green parks, and the vibrant, historic Jewish center of Squirrel Hill.

groceries.name: Murray Avenue Kosher
groceries.description: Fully dedicated kosher supermarket offering fresh glatt kosher meats, deli, bakery, and prepared foods.

attractions.name: Horseshoe Curve
attractions.description: Day trip · about 130 km from Pittsburgh. National Historic Landmark railroad curve (1854) with a visitor center and funicular up to the observation park; kids love watching long freight trains wrap around the bend.

attractions.name: Ohiopyle State Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 75 km from Pittsburgh. 20,500 acres of waterfalls, natural waterslides, and family hiking along the Youghiogheny River Gorge in the Laurel Highlands.

attractions.name: Kamin Science Center
attractions.description: Five floors of interactive science exhibits, the Buhl Planetarium, a giant-screen theater, and a WWII submarine (USS Requin) to tour.

attractions.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
attractions.description: Historic 14-room glasshouse with tropical forest, butterfly room, seasonal flower shows, and the hands-on Discovery Garden for kids.

attractions.name: Duquesne Incline
attractions.description: Ride the historic 1877 cable car (funicular) up Mount Washington for sweeping Pittsburgh skyline and three-rivers views, with a small observation deck and museum at the top.

attractions.name: Children's Museum of Pittsburgh
attractions.description: Hands-on interactive children's museum on Pittsburgh's North Side with exhibits including Waterplay and MAKESHOP. Named #1 Best Children's Museum in America in the USA Today 10Best Readers' Choice 2026 poll.

cities.name: Poconos
cities.description: Majestic Pocono Mountains recreation area featuring lush forests, waterfalls, lakes, and active seasonal Jewish vacation programs.

groceries.name: ShopRite of Stroudsburg
groceries.address: 344 Stroud Mall Rd, Suite 100, Stroudsburg, PA 18360
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.name: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area
attractions.description: 70,000-acre park along the Delaware River with waterfalls, river swim beaches, and hiking trails, including a stretch of the Appalachian Trail.

attractions.name: Steamtown National Historic Site
attractions.description: NPS steam-railroading museum in a historic rail yard with giant locomotives, roundhouse tours, and seasonal train excursions.

cities.name: Providence
cities.description: Rhode Island's vibrant capital pairs rich colonial history, lively riverfront walks, and prominent universities with an active Jewish community.

groceries.name: Eastside Marketplace
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.name: Colt State Park
attractions.description: The "gem" of the RI state park system: 464 acres of groomed waterfront lawns on Narragansett Bay with four miles of paved bike paths, hiking trails, and historic stone walls.

attractions.name: Old Slater Mill
attractions.description: Often called the birthplace of the American Industrial Revolution: Slater Mill, a 1793 water-powered cotton spinning mill on the Blackstone River in Pawtucket, part of Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park. Museum with artifacts, exhibits and guided tours (about 55 minutes).

attractions.name: Roger Williams Park Zoo
attractions.description: Beloved 150-year-old zoo with 130+ species, New England's only Komodo dragon, a zip ride, and the famous Jack-O-Lantern Spectacular each October.

attractions.name: Roger Williams National Memorial
attractions.description: Small NPS site at the spring where Providence was founded in 1636, with exhibits on religious freedom and a Junior Ranger program for kids.

attractions.name: Providence Children's Museum
attractions.description: Hands-on play museum for young children with water-play exhibits and maker studios, among other interactive exhibits.

attractions.name: WaterFire Providence
attractions.description: Iconic free art installation: 80+ bonfires blazing on the downtown rivers with music and performers, on select evenings May through November.

attractions.name: RISD Museum
attractions.description: Eclectic art museum spanning ancient Egyptian artifacts to Impressionist masterpieces; free on Sundays.

attractions.name: Roger Williams Park
attractions.description: 427-acre historic city park (the zoo's home) with lakes, paddle boats, a botanical center, rose gardens, and playgrounds.

cities.name: Newport
cities.description: World-famous sailing capital renowned for dramatic coastal cliffs, historic Gilded Age estates, and deep maritime heritage.

groceries.name: Stop & Shop
groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.description: Rocky coastal preserve at Conanicut Island's southern tip with the historic Beavertail Lighthouse (current tower built 1856, site dates to 1749), tide pools, hiking trails, and scenic sunset views over Narragansett Bay.

attractions.name: Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge
attractions.description: Coastal wildlife refuge in Middletown with more than 2.5 miles of easy, relatively flat ocean-view trails, viewing platforms and a visitor center. It is a stopover and wintering area for migratory birds, and harlequin ducks are often seen in the surf in winter.

attractions.name: Point Judith Lighthouse
attractions.description: Historic 1857 octagonal lighthouse on an active Coast Guard station; the tower and grounds are closed to the public, but it offers sweeping ocean views and great surf-watching from the surrounding area.

attractions.name: Mohegan Bluffs
attractions.description: Clay cliffs rising about 200 feet above Block Island's southern shore. A wooden staircase of roughly 141 steps leads down to a secluded, rocky beach. The bluffs are named for a historic battle on the island.

attractions.name: Southeast Lighthouse
attractions.description: Brick 1875 lighthouse perched above the bluffs, famously moved back from the eroding cliff in 1993; summer tower tours plus a small maritime museum.

attractions.name: The Breakers
attractions.description: The Vanderbilt family's Gilded Age summer "cottage," built between 1893 and 1895. Newport Mansions calls it the grandest of Newport's summer cottages and a symbol of the Vanderbilts' social and financial pre-eminence.

attractions.name: Cliff Walk
attractions.description: Free 3.5-mile oceanfront walkway along the shoreline between crashing waves and the Gilded Age mansions; a National Recreation Trail, open sunrise to sunset year-round.

attractions.name: International Tennis Hall of Fame
attractions.description: Museum tracing the sport's history inside the historic 1880 Newport Casino, home of the first U.S. Championships; kids 12 and under are free.

attractions.name: Fort Adams State Park
attractions.description: Bay-view park around America's largest coastal fortification, with guided fort tours (including underground tunnels), a small beach, picnic grounds, and fishing.

attractions.name: Trustom Pond National Wildlife Refuge
attractions.address: 1040 Matunuck School House Rd, South Kingstown, RI 02879
attractions.description: Rhode Island's only undeveloped coastal salt pond. The 787-acre refuge has about 3 miles of easy trails and habitats including fields, shrublands, woodlands, fresh and saltwater ponds, sandy beaches and dunes. About 300 bird species have been recorded here.

attractions.name: Misquamicut State Beach
attractions.description: Rhode Island's most popular state beach: a half-mile of sand with a playground, concessions, showers, and shade gazebos in the Misquamicut village of Westerly.

attractions.name: Flying Horse Carousel
attractions.description: A historic carousel in Watch Hill (Westerly), RI, often cited as America's oldest continuously operating carousel, dating to the late 1800s; riders can reach for the brass ring during the ride.

cities.name: Charleston

groceries.name: Publix
groceries.description: Carries kosher meats, chicken, turkey, frozen challah and other kosher items, per Congregation Dor Tikvah.

attractions.name: South Carolina Aquarium
attractions.description: Aquarium overlooking Charleston Harbor with thousands of animals, interactive exhibits and many native species, plus the Sea Turtle Care Center, where sick sea turtles are rehabilitated.

attractions.name: Fort Sumter National Monument
attractions.description: Take the ferry out to the Civil War's first-battle fort, with ranger talks and harbor views; departs from the Liberty Square visitor center.

attractions.name: Magnolia Plantation & Gardens
attractions.description: America's oldest public garden, with an Audubon Swamp boardwalk, a wildlife center, and family nature train tours.

attractions.name: Congaree National Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 140 km from Charleston. The largest old-growth bottomland hardwood forest in the U.S., with a 2.4-mile boardwalk loop, canoeing, and free admission just outside Columbia.

attractions.name: Patriots Point Naval & Maritime Museum
attractions.description: Climb aboard the WWII aircraft carrier USS Yorktown, the destroyer USS Laffey, and the Vietnam Experience.

attractions.name: Fort Moultrie
attractions.description: Self-guided walk through 171 years of seacoast defense, from the 1776 palmetto-log fort to WWII, in a unit of Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park.

cities.name: Myrtle Beach

attractions.name: Huntington Beach State Park
attractions.description: 2,500 acres of pristine beach, salt marsh, birdwatching trails, and the Moorish-style Atalaya Castle.

attractions.name: Myrtle Beach

attractions.name: Ripley's Aquarium of Myrtle Beach
attractions.description: Features a shark tunnel, penguin exhibit, stingray touch pools, and a live mermaid show.

cities.name: Hilton Head
cities.description: Tranquil Lowcountry barrier island known for Atlantic beaches, live-oak bike trails, golf courses, and Chabad services.

groceries.name: Food Lion
groceries.description: Carries a large selection of kosher meats, dairy products, and frozen products, per Chabad of Greater Hilton Head.

attractions.name: Coligny Beach Park
attractions.description: The island's most popular oceanfront park: free parking, splash pad, outdoor showers, and wide, gentle beaches steps from Coligny Plaza.

cities.name: Sioux Falls

attractions.description: AZA-accredited zoo with lions, giraffes, tigers, rhinos, and primates, plus a carousel and train for the kids.

attractions.name: Butterfly House & Aquarium
attractions.address: 4320 S Oxbow Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57106
attractions.description: A tropical conservatory with hundreds of free-flying butterflies plus a marine aquarium with touch pools.

attractions.name: Pipestone National Monument

cities.name: Rapid City

groceries.name: Safeway

groceries.description: Supermarket. No Jewish community source confirms a kosher section here; packaged items with a hechsher may be stocked, so call ahead before relying on it.

attractions.description: The world's largest mountain carving in progress, honoring a Lakota leader, with a museum and cultural center on campus in the Black Hills of South Dakota.

attractions.description: Day trip · about 60 km from Rapid City. Ranger-led tours of one of the longest caves on Earth, glittering with calcite crystals and the rare boxwork formations.

attractions.name: Wind Cave National Park

hotels.description: A tranquil 29-acre secluded sanctuary at Punta Nizuc with private mangroves, protected coral reefs, and reflecting pools. Dedicated kosher kitchens with IKM-certified kosher meals for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

attractions.name: Playa Delfines
attractions.description: Spectacular public beach with powdery white sands, expansive Caribbean ocean vistas, and the iconic colorful Cancún photo sign.

attractions.name: Punta Cancún (Hotel Zone & Faro)
attractions.description: The premier northern tip of the Hotel Zone featuring the historic red-and-white Punta Cancún Lighthouse, calm wave-protected turquoise shallows at Playa Caracol, and premier shopping and entertainment.

attractions.name: El Rey Archaeological Zone
attractions.description: Ancient Mayan ruin site situated right inside the Cancun Hotel Zone, featuring 47 excavated structures including a pyramid-shaped temple dating to around 250 A.D.

attractions.name: Isla Mujeres
attractions.description: Small Caribbean island about 13 km off the coast of Cancun. It is reached by a roughly 20-minute ferry from Puerto Juárez or the Hotel Zone, and offers beaches and an underwater museum.

destinations.name: Cozumel
destinations.description: A world-class diving destination characterized by breathtaking coral reefs, crystalline waters, and a very popular Jewish traveler community.

chabad.name: Chabad of Cozumel

restaurants.address: 5a Avenida Sur, C. 1 Sur y, Centro, 77668 Cozumel, Q.R., Mexico
restaurants.kashrus: Chabad of Cozumel (mashgiach temidi; pas Yisrael, chalav Yisrael, Beit Yosef meat)

restaurants.name: Chocolatte Espresso Bar - Kosher
restaurants.kind: Dairy Cafe / Espresso Bar / Sandwiches & Salads

restaurants.name: Fuego Restaurant Cozumel
restaurants.address: 125 Av. Rafael E. Melgar, between Calle 2 & Calle 4, Cozumel

groceries.name: Chabad Cozumel Kosher Grocery Store
groceries.address: 5a Avenida Sur, between Calle 1 Sur and Adolfo Rosado Salas, Centro, San Miguel de Cozumel
groceries.description: Kosher meat (steaks, ground beef, chicken, sausages), cheeses and dairy, snacks, Shabbat and holiday products; Sun–Thu 10 am–10 pm; +52 987 104 0770.

groceries.name: Chabad Cozumel Bakery
groceries.address: At Chabad of Cozumel, 5a Avenida Sur, Centro, Cozumel
groceries.description: Parve kosher bakery: challahs, breads, cakes and desserts, under Chabad of Cozumel.

hotels.name: Casa Mexicana Cozumel
hotels.address: Av. Rafael E. Melgar 457, Centro, 77600 San Miguel de Cozumel, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Vibrant, charming waterfront boutique hotel located on the San Miguel malecón with a tranquil oceanfront plunge pool terrace. The absolute top choice for Shabbat-observant travelers on Cozumel due to its short walking distance to Chabad.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 0.6 km (8-minute walk) from Chabad of Cozumel and Alma Kosher on 5a Avenida Sur; Chocolatte and Fuego kosher are within about 0.7 km. Rooms have a small refrigerator. Chabad of Cozumel lists it as a recommended hotel.

hotels.name: Presidente InterContinental Cozumel Resort & Spa
hotels.address: Carr. Chankanaab Km 6.5, Zona Hotelera Sur, 77600 Cozumel, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: The premier 5-star luxury resort on the island, boasting an extraordinary private marine reef, secluded ocean coves, and private dive boat pick-up directly from its pier.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 6 km south of Chabad of Cozumel downtown; taxi needed, not walkable for Shabbat.

hotels.name: The Westin Cozumel
hotels.address: Carretera Costera Norte Km 4.8, 77613 Cozumel, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Modern, high-rise luxury hotel with magnificent ocean views on Cozumel’s tranquil northern coast, featuring private plunge pool cabanas, rooftop sky lounge, and water sports.
hotels.kosherNotes: Rooms have a mini fridge. About 5 km north of Chabad of Cozumel downtown; taxi needed, not walkable for Shabbat.

hotels.name: Hotel B Cozumel
hotels.address: Carretera Costera Norte Km 2.5, Zona Hotelera Norte, 77600 Cozumel, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Boutique oceanfront retreat combining chic Mexican artisanal design with seaside hammocks, an oceanfront hot tub, and direct snorkeling access into a thriving coral lagoon.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 3 km from Chabad of Cozumel (roughly a 45-minute walk along the coast road, or a short taxi). Rooms have a mini fridge (guest report).

attractions.name: Palancar Reef
attractions.description: World-renowned marine sanctuary along the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, celebrated for towering coral pinnacles, deep swim-through caves, and crystal-clear underwater visibility.

attractions.name: Chankanaab Beach Adventure Park
attractions.description: Adventure park inside Cozumel's National Reef Marine Park with a beach, a lagoon, reef snorkeling and scuba diving, a tropical garden, prehispanic replicas, a Mayan hut and a kids' playground. Some activities, such as dolphin swims, cost extra.

attractions.name: Punta Sur Ecological Park
attractions.description: Protected ecological reserve at Cozumel's southern tip, home to the historic Celarain lighthouse, crocodile observation towers on Colombia Lagoon, and white-sand beaches.

attractions.name: Villa Maya Nature Reserve
attractions.description: Lush private ecological reserve nestled in Cozumel’s interior jungle along Camino a Villa Maya, dedicated to rainforest conservation, native biodiversity, and peaceful nature walks.

attractions.name: Zona Arqueológica San Gervasio
attractions.description: Ancient pre-Columbian Mayan archaeological site on Cozumel, long considered a pilgrimage center dedicated to the goddess Ixchel, with several Mayan structures to explore amid island wildlife.

attractions.name: Benito Juárez Park (Parque Benito Juárez)
attractions.description: Central waterfront plaza and gathering point in downtown San Miguel de Cozumel, steps from the ferry terminal, with a historic clock tower, a shaded gazebo, a fountain, benches and the colorful COZUMEL sign, surrounded by shops, cafés and restaurants.

attractions.name: Parque Andrés Quintana Roo (Parque Municipal)
attractions.description: Spacious civic park in Cozumel with a monument to independence figure Andrés Quintana Roo, open-air event pavilions, tree-lined walking areas, spaces where children play, and lively evening gatherings with live music and local island atmosphere.

destinations.name: Playa del Carmen
destinations.description: A chic, trendy coastal resort town on the Riviera Maya, combining beautiful Caribbean coastlines with lively dining, eco-adventure parks, and a welcoming Chabad house.

chabad.address: 20 Avenida Nte. S/N, entre Calle 2 y Benito Juárez, Centro, 77710 Playa del Carmen, Q.R., Mexico

restaurants.kashrus: Rabbi Nigri (as Chabad Playa's list states)

restaurants.description: Kosher meat restaurant on 5th Avenue; open Sun–Thu 1–11 pm, Fri 1–4 pm (per Chabad).

restaurants.description: Dairy Mediterranean restaurant near Mamitas beach.

restaurants.description: Kosher grill; Sun–Thu 2–10:30 pm, Fri 10 am–3 pm (per Chabad).

restaurants.description: Kosher steakhouse on 20 Avenida, the street of the Chabad House.

restaurants.name: Yummi Lawaj
restaurants.description: Dairy spot with seating and delivery.

groceries.address: Calle 8 Norte & Av. 20, Centro, Playa del Carmen
groceries.description: Kosher bakery under American Kosher supervision. Phone +52 984 167 5590.

groceries.address: Av. 20 Norte between Av. Juárez and Calle 2, Centro, Playa del Carmen
groceries.description: Kosher market run with Chabad of Playa del Carmen. Phone +52 984 106 3122. Open Sun–Thu 8 am–11 pm, Fri 8 am–5 pm, Saturday night 7–11 pm.

groceries.name: Shabbat & holiday meals to go
groceries.address: 2 Avenida Benito Juárez, Playa del Carmen
groceries.description: Ready-made meat and parve Shabbat/holiday food to order; WhatsApp +52 984 183 2028 (listed by Chabad).

hotels.name: Devossion by Live Aqua Playa del Carmen
hotels.address: 1a Avenida Esquina Calle 26, Col. Centro, 77710 Playa del Carmen, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Adults-only, all-inclusive beachfront resort (formerly the Grand Hyatt Playa del Carmen, rebranded in 2025) on the beach at Calle 26 in downtown Playa del Carmen, a short walk from 5th Avenue and Mamitas Beach. Pools, spa and several à la carte restaurants. Note: guests must be adults (no children), and the all-inclusive dining is not kosher.
hotels.kosherNotes: Adults-only all-inclusive, so not for families with children. About 1.6 km (roughly a 22-minute walk) from Chabad of Playa del Carmen on 20 Avenida; Hilula kosher bakery is about 1.2 km.

hotels.name: The Fives Downtown Hotel & Residences, Curio Collection by Hilton
hotels.address: Avenida 10 Norte entre Calle 2 y 4, Centro, 77710 Playa del Carmen, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Chic, modern urban residential hotel located on 10th Avenue in the heart of downtown Playa del Carmen, featuring residential suites with full kitchenettes and a stunning rooftop infinity pool lounge overlooking the Caribbean.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 0.3 km (5-minute walk) from Chabad of Playa del Carmen on 20 Avenida. Suites have a kitchen with stove, microwave and refrigerator; some units have full-size refrigerators.

hotels.name: The St. Regis Kanai Resort, Riviera Maya
hotels.address: Paseo Kanai 15, Solidaridad, 77730 Playa del Carmen, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Architectural marvel elevated on stilted circular pavilions over a 620-acre mangrove reserve with private plunge pools, beach cabanas, and signature St. Regis butler service.
hotels.kosherNotes: Kosher meals can be ordered through the hotel from an outside certified kosher caterer (traveler reports). About 14 km from Chabad of Playa del Carmen; not walkable for Shabbat.

hotels.name: Banyan Tree Mayakoba
hotels.address: Carretera Federal Chetumal-Puerto Juárez Km 298, 77710 Playa del Carmen, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Ultra-exclusive private villa estate situated along tranquil emerald waterways and mangroves in Mayakoba. Every villa features a private heated plunge pool, lush walled gardens, and boat-accessible waterways.
hotels.kosherNotes: All-pool-villa resort. Banyan Tree has offered kosher meals through The Ember, its kosher menu (hotel PDF, 2022); confirm it still runs. About 8 km from Chabad of Playa del Carmen; not walkable for Shabbat.

attractions.name: Quinta Avenida (5th Avenue)
attractions.description: Lively pedestrian-only street in Playa del Carmen running parallel to the beach for over 4 km, lined with shops, cafes, restaurants, fashion boutiques, art galleries and artisan stalls.

attractions.name: Cenote Azul
attractions.description: Breathtaking open-air freshwater limestone pool bordered by jungle limestone ledges, crystal-clear turquoise waters, natural cliff-jumping perches, and friendly nibbling fish.

attractions.name: Cenote Cristalino
attractions.description: Natural cenote near Playa del Carmen with clear water, a cave, and a popular swimming and snorkeling spot.

attractions.name: Cenote Chaak Tun
attractions.description: Underground cenote cave system near Playa del Carmen featuring stalactites and stalagmites, explored on guided snorkeling tours through low-lit caverns and natural pools.

attractions.name: Nearby Tulum Archaeological Ruins (Day-Trip)
attractions.description: 13th-century walled Mayan city on 12-meter (about 40-foot) cliffs overlooking the turquoise Caribbean Sea, roughly a 45-minute to one-hour drive south of Playa del Carmen.

attractions.name: Xcaret Park
attractions.description: World-class eco-archaeological theme park celebrating Mexico’s rich folklore, subterranean river swimming, butterfly pavilions, coral aquariums, and the celebrated México Espectacular evening performance.

destinations.name: Tulum
destinations.description: A trendy, boho-chic seaside escape famous for preserved Mayan cliffside ruins, luxurious eco-resorts, yoga retreats, and a warm Jewish community offering Shabbat options.
destinations.airport: Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (TQO) / Cancún Airport (CUN)

chabad.name: Chabad of Tulum

restaurants.kashrus: Kosher dairy (Chabad Tulum's café, as Chabad Tulum states it)

hotels.name: Dreams Tulum Resort & Spa
hotels.address: Puerto Juarez, Carretera Chetumal Km. 236, 77760 Tulum, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Secluded Spanish hacienda-style beachfront resort nestled on an expansive powdery white sand bay north of the Tulum ruins, featuring traditional Mexican arches, palm groves, and quiet oceanfront pools.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 9 km north of Chabad of Tulum; taxi needed, not walkable for Shabbat.

hotels.name: Hotel Bardo Tulum
hotels.address: Rio Otate & Rio Basca, 77760 Tulum, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Adults-only mystical jungle sanctuary located in tranquil La Veleta, featuring secluded loft-style villas with private stone plunge pools, lush gardens, outdoor showers, and an ambient firepit lounge.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 1.5 km (roughly an 18-minute walk) from Chabad of Tulum on Av. Kukulkan in La Veleta.

hotels.name: Be Tulum (BE DESTINATION Tulum)
hotels.address: Carretera Tulum-Boca Paila Km 10, Zona Hotelera, 77780 Tulum, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Chic barefoot-luxury jungle resort constructed with native stone, reclaimed wood, and limestone on Tulum’s south beach road, featuring rooftop plunge pools and oceanfront daybeds.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 7.5 km from Chabad of Tulum via the beach road; taxi needed, not walkable for Shabbat.

hotels.name: La Valise Tulum
hotels.address: Carr. Tulum-Boca Paila Km 8.7, Tulum Beach, Zona Hotelera, 77760 Tulum, Q.R., Mexico
hotels.description: Exclusive 11-room boutique beachfront sanctuary famous for handcrafted artisan suites with open-air master beds that roll out onto private oceanfront terraces overlooking the Caribbean.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 7 km from Chabad of Tulum; not walkable for Shabbat.

attractions.name: Tulum Archaeological Site
attractions.description: Ancient Mayan walled city dramatically perched on high limestone cliffs above the sea.

attractions.name: Gran Cenote
attractions.description: Famous half-cavern cenote populated by friendly freshwater turtles and small bats.

attractions.name: Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve
attractions.description: Massive UNESCO World Heritage site featuring wild dolphins, manatees, and wetlands.

destinations.name: Cabo San Lucas
destinations.description: A spectacular desert-meets-ocean destination at the southern tip of the Baja Peninsula, offering dramatic rock formations, luxury golf resorts, and an active Chabad catering to Jewish tourists.

restaurants.description: Glatt-kosher meat restaurant on the ground floor of the Cabo Jewish Center: burgers, schnitzel, ribeye, fish tacos; delivers to hotels; Shabbat catering. Sun–Thu 1–9 pm, Fri 10 am–3 pm.
restaurants.kashrus: Rabbi Benny Hershcovich, Chabad of Cabo

restaurants.name: The Bagel Spot
restaurants.address: Cabo Jewish Center (2nd floor), Camino de la Plaza 135, Pedregal, Cabo San Lucas
restaurants.description: Coffee, bagel sandwiches, pizza, salads and smoothies; delivers to hotels in and around Cabo. Sun–Thu 8 am–3 pm, Fri 10–3.
restaurants.kashrus: Rabbi Benny Hershcovich, Chabad of Cabo

groceries.name: Kosher Meat Freezer at the Cabo Jewish Center
groceries.address: Camino de la Plaza 135, Pedregal, Cabo San Lucas (ground floor)
groceries.description: Glatt kosher meat and chicken for sale (bringing meat into Mexico is not allowed); special orders 2 weeks ahead.

groceries.name: Chedraui Selecto / Soriana (kosher-symbol products)
groceries.description: Chabad of Cabo lists kosher-symbol basics found in these supermarkets (e.g. MK tuna, OK frozen bagels at Chedraui); it does not vouch for the symbols.

hotels.name: Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal
hotels.address: Cam. del Mar 1, Pedregal, 23455 Cabo San Lucas, B.C.S., Mexico
hotels.description: Spectacular 5-star ultra-luxury resort carved into towering granite cliffs at Land’s End, entered through a private torch-lit chandelier tunnel piercing the mountain. Every room features a private plunge pool, panoramic Pacific ocean views, and personal concierge service. The premier choice for Shabbat travelers due to its walking proximity to Chabad.
hotels.kosherNotes: About 0.75 km (roughly a 10-minute walk by map routing) from the Cabo Jewish Center / Chabad of Cabo at Camino de la Plaza 135, Pedregal.

hotels.name: Zadún, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve
hotels.address: Blvd. Mar de Cortez, 23403 San José del Cabo, B.C.S., Mexico
hotels.description: Ultra-luxurious coastal sanctuary set where dramatic desert bluffs meet the Sea of Cortez, offering breathtaking desert-meets-ocean scenery. Standalone ocean-view pavilions each feature a private plunge pool and dedicated Tosoani private butler. Seasonal whale watching is frequently visible directly from private room terraces.
hotels.kosherNotes: Beyond Kosher Experience: separate meat and dairy kitchens supervised by Chabad of Cabo (K-abo Kosher), glatt meat, cholov Yisroel dairy, Shabbat menu. Mashgiach fee $200/day paid to Chabad; book at least 72 hours ahead. About 34 km from Cabo San Lucas.

hotels.name: Solaz, a Luxury Collection Resort, Los Cabos
hotels.address: KM 18.5 Carretera Transpeninsular CSL-SJC, Tourist Corridor, 23405 San José del Cabo, B.C.S., Mexico
hotels.description: Contemporary architectural resort along the Tourist Corridor featuring an on-site certified kosher culinary program, cascading infinity pools, private ocean terraces, and multi-bedroom residences and suites with full kitchens and kitchenettes.
hotels.kosherNotes: On-site kosher program: breakfast at Cascabel, dairy lunch at Riccio di Mare, meat dinner at Mako, plus Shabbat meals. For Shabbat, room motion sensors (lights, A/C) and the electronic door lock can be turned off on request.

attractions.name: El Arco & Land’s End (The Arch of Cabo San Lucas)
attractions.description: Iconic granite archway standing 200 feet tall where the Sea of Cortez meets the Pacific Ocean, best experienced via glass-bottom boat tour.

attractions.name: Playa del Amor (Lover’s Beach) & Pelican Rock
attractions.description: Secluded beach nestled between towering granite cliffs, accessible only by water taxi or boat, popular for snorkeling and swimming.

attractions.name: Playa El Médano (Medano Beach)
attractions.description: Cabo's main safe-swimming beach, known for gentle waves, water sports like paddleboarding, and beachfront views toward El Arco.

attractions.name: Chileno Bay & Santa Maria Beach
attractions.description: Chileno Bay and Santa Maria Beach are two Blue Flag beaches on the Tourist Corridor near Cabo San Lucas. Both bays are sheltered from strong waves, with calm, clear water popular for swimming and snorkeling. Chileno Bay has showers and restrooms.

attractions.name: Marina Cabo San Lucas Boardwalk
attractions.description: Yacht harbor and marina in Cabo San Lucas with a pedestrian boardwalk lined with shops, restaurants, and sunset tour boats.

attractions.name: Mount Solmar & Cerro del Vigía
attractions.description: Dramatic granite peak above Land’s End offering an exhilarating desert ridge hike with 360-degree ocean panoramas.

attractions.name: Mercado Orgánico San José & Mercado Popular
attractions.description: Organic market in San José del Cabo (at Club La Huerta) with local crafts, produce, food stalls, and handmade goods, held on Saturdays.

attractions.name: Cabo Pulmo National Marine Park
attractions.description: Day trip · about 95 km from Cabo San Lucas. National marine park on the east coast of the Baja California Peninsula. It protects the northernmost coral reef in the eastern Pacific, estimated at about 20,000 years old. Known for snorkeling and diving.

destinations.name: Mexico City
destinations.description: A colossal historical metropolis and global culinary powerhouse. For Jewish travelers, Mexico City features a massive, incredibly prosperous community centered in the Polanco neighborhood, with dozens of top-tier kosher restaurants and markets.

attractions.name: Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec)
attractions.description: Historic hilltop castle overlooking Chapultepec Forest, one of only two royal palaces in North America once inhabited by monarchs (Emperor Maximilian I & Empress Carlota), now home to the National Museum of History.

attractions.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
attractions.description: Premier world-class museum in Chapultepec showcasing profound pre-Columbian civilizations, featuring the monumental Aztec Sun Stone calendar.

attractions.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
attractions.description: Dramatic marble performance hall and museum in central Mexico City, featuring murals by Diego Rivera among other artists.

attractions.name: Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL)
attractions.description: Architectural jewel on Calle de Tacuba housing five centuries of Mexican artistic heritage from the viceregal colonial era through 20th-century masters inside a regal neoclassical palace.

attractions.name: Palacio de Minería
attractions.description: Neoclassical building in Mexico City's Centro Histórico, designed and built between 1797 and 1813 by Valencian sculptor and architect Manuel Tolsá to house the Royal School of Mines. Now part of UNAM's Faculty of Engineering, it houses the Tolsá Museum and temporary exhibitions.

attractions.name: Casa de los Azulejos (The House of Tiles)
attractions.description: Exquisite 18th-century baroque count's residence whose exterior facade is covered on three sides in hand-painted blue-and-white Talavera ceramic tiles from Puebla.

attractions.name: Plaza de la Constitución (El Zócalo)
attractions.description: Monumental central square and ceremonial bedrock of Mexico City, bordered by the National Palace and the buried foundations of ancient Tenochtitlan.

attractions.name: Xochimilco Canals (Embarcadero Nativitas)
attractions.description: UNESCO World Heritage canal network in Xochimilco, navigated by colorful trajinera boats departing from Embarcadero Nuevo Nativitas, one of the main boat launches offering tours past floating gardens and chinampas.

attractions.name: Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela
attractions.description: Long-running artisan market on Balderas in Mexico City's Centro, with about 350 vendors selling folk art and handicrafts from around Mexico, including alebrijes, Otomi textiles, jewelry and traditional clothing. Free entry.

attractions.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (The Blue House)
attractions.description: Cobalt-blue house museum in Coyoacán, birthplace and lifelong home of Frida Kahlo. Preserves her personal belongings, artwork by Kahlo and Diego Rivera, folk art, and pre-Hispanic artifacts.

eruv.description: Mexico City has eruvin in the Jewish neighborhoods (Polanco, Lomas, Tecamachalco). Before Shabbat, confirm the eruv is up for the week (Chabad of Mexico: WhatsApp +52 56 2452 1110). Communal Shabbat dinners are hosted at Chabad CDMX - Polanco (advance RSVP required).
